advances: A local upper-cover argument for ordinary uniform maximal depth under an actual full critical circuit. It yields a derivative of the cover bound and uses equality at the starting body. It supplies no bound for the locked mixed-integer problem.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The original cuts are proper because $0\in\operatorname{int}K$, so every $S_i>0$. For every $y\ne0$, spanning and the positive dependence give some $u_i\cdot y>0$. The corresponding cap through $y$ is strictly smaller than its central cap because shifting the threshold by any positive distance removes positive volume near the proper central section. Thus the assumed maximal raw depth $Q$ is attained at $0$, where the selected caps have mass $Q$. In the everywhere positive-curvature case, minimality rules out an antipodal pair, which would be a positive dependence on a proper subset of the $d+1$ normals. No unoriented plane class can then cancel its positive weights. By the crossing argument in the bump lemma there is a signature patch with $W\ne\Phi(K)=Q/|K|$, giving an eligible bump. In the local version this property is assumed of the selected bump.

The lemma places the entire changed shell at a fixed positive distance from the planes for all sufficiently small signed $t$. Thus for thresholds $b$ sufficiently close to $0$,
$$
|K_t\cap\{x:u_i\cdot x\ge b\}|=F_i(b)+e_i\Delta V(t),
\qquad
F_i(b)=|K\cap\{x:u_i\cdot x\ge b\}|.
$$
Let $A_i(s)=\mathcal H^{d-1}(K\cap\{x:u_i\cdot x=s\})$. Since $u_i$ is unit, Fubini in the coordinates $x=z+su_i$ with $z\in u_i^\perp$ gives
$$
F_i(b)=\int_b^\infty A_i(s)\,ds.
$$
The slice area $A_i(s)$ is continuous at every proper threshold. Indeed, translate the slices to $u_i^\perp$ and apply dominated convergence to their indicators on a common bounded projection of $K$. The indicators converge off the relative boundary of the limiting slice, which has measure zero in the plane. Its relative interior lies in $\operatorname{int}K$ because any supporting hyperplane there would have to contain the cutting plane, which meets $\operatorname{int}K$. Thus $F_i'(b)=-A_i(b)$ continuously for $b$ near $0$, and $F_i'(0)=-S_i$.

Solve the $d+1$ equations
$$
F_i(u_i\cdot y(t))+e_i\Delta V(t)=q(t),\qquad y(0)=0,\quad q(0)=Q.
$$
The offset formula and the bump lemma give a $C^1$ system. Its Jacobian in $(y,q)$ at the base point has rows $(-S_i u_i^\top,-1)$. If $(v,r)$ belongs to its kernel, multiplying the rows by $\theta_i$ and summing gives $r=0$ by the coarea balance. The normals span and $S_i>0$, so $v=0$. The implicit function theorem therefore supplies a local $C^1$ solution. Differentiating the equations at zero and taking their $\theta_i$-weighted sum yields $q'(0)=W V'_0$. Dividing by $V_t$ gives the stated derivative.

For any $x\in\mathbb R^d$, the margins $u_i\cdot(x-y(t))$ cannot all be negative, because their weighted sum with positive weights $\theta_i S_i$ is zero. At least one closed cap through $y(t)$ therefore contains $x$. Its mass is $q(t)$, which bounds the raw depth of $x$ from above. At $t=0$ the normalized cover bound equals the actual maximum $Q/|K|$ by hypothesis. Its nonzero derivative and $V'_0>0$ give strict decrease of that maximum for $t>0$ if $W<Q/|K|$ and $t<0$ if $W>Q/|K|$. The section identities concern the original fixed planes, while the cover uses their parallel translates.
statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with $0\in\operatorname{int}K$. Suppose the $d+1$ unit vectors $u_i$ span $\mathbb R^d$ and form a minimal positive circuit, and that $\theta_i>0$, $\sum_i\theta_i=1$ satisfy $\sum_i\theta_i S_i u_i=0$, where $S_i=\mathcal H^{d-1}(K\cap u_i^\perp)$. As in the stationary setting, suppose the sections have centroid $0$. Assume the central cap masses $|K\cap\{x:u_i\cdot x\ge0\}|$ all equal $Q$, where $Q$ is the maximum over $y\in K$ of $\inf_{H\ni y}|K\cap H|$ for closed halfspaces $H$. Then the selected caps attain the depth at the deepest point $0$.

Take a bump $K_t$ as in the section-preserving support-bump lemma with signature weight $W\ne Q/|K|$. Such a bump exists if $h$ is $C^2$ with everywhere positive-definite $A_h$. For small signed $t$ there are a point $y(t)$ near $0$ and $d+1$ parallel translates of the respective original caps through $y(t)$, all with the same mass $q(t)$. They cover $\mathbb R^d$ and bound the new maximum raw depth by $q(t)$. The normalized cover bound has derivative
$$
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\frac{q(t)}{|K_t|}\right|_{t=0}
=\left(W-\frac Q{|K|}\right)\frac{V'_0}{|K|}.
$$
For all sufficiently small nonzero $t$ of the appropriate sign, the maximal normalized ordinary depth of $K_t$ is strictly below that of $K$.
title: A section-preserving bump decreases maximal ordinary depth for a full critical circuit
